comment: @spec AUTOMATED-REMEDIATION-5 @spec AUTOMATED-REMEDIATION-6 @spec AUTOMATED-REMEDIATION-7 @spec AUTOMATED-REMEDIATION-26. The nomination block grammar, frozen between the protected worker's capture wrapper and the API's nomination parser, which ship in different images. A block opens with a line that is exactly `opening_fence` and closes with a line that is exactly `closing_fence`; lines end at `line_terminator`. Each case gives the turn's final `output` and `status`, and optionally the `deltas` it streamed in (their concatenation is `output`; without `deltas` a reader may split `output` anywhere). Worker side: the streaming line filter over the deltas and the `Final` capture both yield `reply` (every line from an opening fence line through its closing fence line withheld, an unclosed block withheld to the end, in every status); `submitted` is the exact withheld text the worker posts for a turn whose status is in `submit_statuses`, or null when it posts nothing. API side: `parse` is the parser's result on `submitted` (null when nothing is submitted): `valid` with one entry per nomination in order (`arguments` is the canonical text of action-canonical-arguments.json and its SHA-256; `reason` null when absent; `refusal` `duplicate_code` for a later entry naming the same action and canonical arguments, else null), or `malformed` (the whole block refused `malformed_code`). `max_block_bytes` bounds the submitted text in UTF-8 bytes, fence lines included. A `change` shaped entry (a tune nomination, AUTOMATED-REMEDIATION-25) parses to arguments that are the canonical {field, rule, value} object. Read by apps/worker/tests/test_remediation_nomination_vector.py and apps/api/tests/test_remediation_nomination_vector.py, each of which rejects an unknown key.
